name: Single-Arm Cable Lateral Raise
summary: An isolation exercise that uses a low cable pulley to target the lateral deltoid with continuous resistance throughout the movement.

setup: Set the cable pulley to its lowest position and attach a single D-handle.
Stand sideways to the pulley with your feet hip-width apart.
Reach across your body with the outside arm to grip the handle with a neutral or overhand grip.
Stand tall with a slight bend in the working elbow and hold the machine upright with your non-working hand for balance.
steps: Raise your working arm out to the side in a smooth arc until your elbow and hand are at shoulder height.
Pause briefly at the top to contract the lateral deltoid.
Lower the cable slowly under control back across your body to the starting position.
Complete the desired reps, then turn around and repeat with the other arm.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you raise the cable out to the side; inhale as you lower it back down.
cues: Keep the wrist relaxed and below the elbow.
Stay upright without leaning or swinging.

common_faults.fault: Swinging the torso to generate momentum.
common_faults.correction: Reduce the weight and hold the upright cable post to anchor your body in place.

common_faults.fault: Shrugging the shoulder excessively with the upper traps.
common_faults.correction: Keep your shoulder blade depressed and focus on driving the elbow outward rather than upward.

common_faults.fault: Raising the arm well above shoulder level.
common_faults.correction: Stop when your upper arm reaches roughly parallel to the floor to keep tension on the deltoid.

precautions: Keep the working elbow soft, never hyperextended, to protect the elbow joint.
